fields.Participants: Market Research Analyst, CMO, VP Store Operations

workflows.name: Quarterly Customer Satisfaction (CSAT) Survey Design & Execution

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-validate of "checkout speed, pricing competitiveness, product quality, returns experience" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-identify of "identify top 10 improvement themes" (replaces manual Step 3).
- System auto-assign of "assign action items to relevant departments with timelines" (replaces manual Step 4).
Controls: - operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Response bias**: Satisfied customers are more likely to respond; dissatisfied customers may not; supplement with in-store intercept and post-return surveys for balanced data
Staffing Implication: - **Market Research Analyst**: CSAT survey adds ~3 weeks/quarter = ~12 weeks/year — absorbed if dedicated role; otherwise outsourced (~PHP 200K–400K/quarter to research agency)
System Touchpoints: - Survey platform integrated with loyalty/CRM for distribution (W1902.2)
- CSAT analytics dashboard with trend and driver analysis (W1902.3)
- Action item tracking linked to department KPIs (W1902.4)
- Integration with W13.1 (customer complaints), W67 (store performance), W1550 (VOC analysis)

steps.activity: Market Research Analyst designs CSAT survey instrument: (a) overall satisfaction: "How satisfied are you with your recent BuildRight experience?" (1–5 scale), (b) satisfaction drivers: product availability, store cleanliness, staff helpfulness, checkout speed, pricing competitiveness, product quality, returns experience, (c) open-ended: "What could BuildRight do to improve your experience?", (d) segment questions: DIY homeowner vs. trade professional vs. corporate buyer, (e) channel: email to loyalty members, SMS to recent POS customers, in-store tablet survey at exit

Survey distribution: (a) email survey to random sample of 10,000 loyalty members per quarter, (b) SMS survey to 5,000 recent POS customers (purchase in last 30 days), (c) in-store tablet at 20 stores (rotated quarterly) for exit survey, (d) incentive: 50 loyalty points for completion; target response rate ≥ 15%

Analysis: (a) overall CSAT score by quarter and trend, (b) CSAT by store cluster and region, (c) CSAT by customer segment (DIY, trade, corporate), (d) driver analysis: which satisfaction drivers have the strongest correlation with overall CSAT?, (e) text analytics on open-ended responses: identify top 10 improvement themes, (f) statistical significance testing for quarter-over-quarter changes

Presentation and action planning: (a) CMO presents findings to VP Store Operations and VP Merchandising, (b) identify top 3 improvement priorities per quarter, (c) assign action items to relevant departments with timelines, (d) track action item completion for next quarter's survey

fields.Participants: Market Research Analyst, CMO, VP Store Operations

workflows.name: Net Promoter Score (NPS) Monthly Measurement & Trend Analysis

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-send of "sends NPS survey to random sample of customers within 48 hours of purchase" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-identify of "identify stores or segments with declining NPS for targeted intervention" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System workflow notification of "contact Detractors who provided contact information to address their issues per…" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-373 (ensure controlled execution — Customer Satisfaction & Experience Research (PA-44.1).)
- operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Survey fatigue**: Monthly NPS surveys may annoy frequent shoppers (trade professionals buying weekly); throttle survey frequency per customer to max once per quarter
Staffing Implication: - No incremental headcount — absorbed by Market Research Analyst
System Touchpoints: - Automated NPS survey distribution triggered by purchase event (W1903.1)
- NPS analytics with segmentation and trend tracking (W1903.2)
- Detractor "close the loop" workflow integrated with W13.1 (W1903.3d)
- Integration with W13 (customer experience), W67 (store performance), W1550 (VOC analysis)

steps.activity: Monthly: system sends NPS survey to random sample of customers within 48 hours of purchase: (a) single question: "On a scale of 0–10, how likely are you to recommend BuildRight to a friend or colleague?", (b) follow-up: "What is the primary reason for your score?", (c) classification: Promoters (9–10), Passives (7–8), Detractors (0–6), (d) NPS = % Promoters − % Detractors

Monthly analysis: (a) overall NPS score and trend, (b) NPS by store, region, and customer segment, (c) NPS by purchase channel (in-store, ecommerce, B2B), (d) theme analysis of verbatim responses, (e) identify stores or segments with declining NPS for targeted intervention

Quarterly: CMO presents NPS trend to executive team: (a) target NPS: ≥ 50 (good) → ≥ 70 (excellent) for Philippine retail, (b) benchmark against Philippine retail industry NPS (if available), (c) correlation analysis: NPS vs. same-store sales growth, (d) "close the loop": contact Detractors who provided contact information to address their issues per W13.1

fields.Participants: Market Research Analyst, VP Store Operations, VP Merchandising
fields.Volume: Touchpoints: returns, special orders, BOPIS pickup, delivery, complaints

workflows.name: Customer Effort Score (CES) Measurement for Key Service Touchpoints

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-schedule of "schedule and receive your delivery?" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-identify of "identify touchpoints with CES < 5" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-review of "reviews low-CES touchpoints" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-373 (ensure controlled execution — Customer Satisfaction & Experience Research (PA-44.1).)
- operational: Market Research Analyst review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Low response rate for post-service surveys**: Customers who complete a return or complaint are often eager to leave; those with smooth experiences may not respond; low response rates skew data
System Touchpoints: - CES survey triggered by service interaction type (W1904.1)
- CES analytics by touchpoint and store (W1904.2)
- Integration with W12 (returns), W11 (BOPIS), W19 (delivery), W13.1 (complaints), W38 (special orders)

steps.activity: System triggers CES survey after key service interactions: (a) returns: "How easy was it to return your item today?" (1–7 scale, 1 = very difficult, 7 = very easy), (b) BOPIS pickup: "How easy was it to pick up your online order?", (c) delivery: "How easy was it to schedule and receive your delivery?", (d) complaint resolution: "How easy was it to resolve your issue?", (e) special order: "How easy was it to place and receive your special order?"

Monthly analysis: (a) CES by touchpoint and trend, (b) identify touchpoints with CES < 5 (high effort = poor experience): priority for process improvement, (c) CES by store for returns and BOPIS (identifies stores with poor service execution), (d) correlate CES with repeat purchase behavior

Quarterly: VP Store Operations reviews low-CES touchpoints: (a) identify root cause of high customer effort, (b) implement process improvements to reduce effort (simplify return process, improve BOPIS pickup signage, streamline complaint resolution), (c) track CES improvement post-intervention

fields.Participants: Market Research Analyst, Research Agency (field interviewers), VP Store Operations
fields.Volume: ~500–1,000 intercept interviews across 10 stores per cycle

workflows.name: In-Store Customer Intercept Survey & Shopper Journey Mapping

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-validate of "Market Research Analyst designs intercept survey and shopper journey" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-track of "track shopper movement patterns through store" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-review of "VP Store Operations and VP Merchandising review findings" (replaces manual Step 4).
Controls: - CTL-373 (ensure controlled execution — Customer Satisfaction & Experience Research (PA-44.1).)
- operational: Market Research Analyst review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Sample bias**: Exit intercepts only capture customers who visited the store, not potential customers who chose competitors; supplement with non-customer research for competitive insight
System Touchpoints: - Shopper journey mapping analytics (W1905.3a)
- Department conversion analytics from POS data (W1905.3b)
- Heatmap visualization of store traffic patterns (W1905.2c)
- Integration with W67 (store performance), W1848 (planogram), W1116 (complaint trend analysis)

steps.activity: Market Research Analyst designs intercept survey and shopper journey study: (a) shopper profile: purpose of visit, frequency, companion type, time spent in store, (b) journey mapping: which departments did they visit? In what order? What was their path through the store?, (c) conversion: did they find what they were looking for? If not, why? Did they buy anything?, (d) basket analysis: what did they buy vs. what they intended to buy?, (e) store experience: signage clarity, department navigation, staff interaction quality, checkout experience, (f) competitor comparison: where else do they shop for home improvement? Why?

Execute fieldwork: (a) engage research agency for trained interviewers at 10 stores (5 urban, 5 provincial), (b) 2-week data collection: intercept customers at store exit, (c) observational component: track shopper movement patterns through store (heatmap analysis)

Analysis: (a) shopper journey maps: typical paths for DIY vs. trade customers, (b) conversion rate by department: what % of visitors to each department make a purchase?, (c) friction points: where do customers get frustrated or leave without buying?, (d) cross-shop analysis: which competitor stores do BuildRight customers also visit?, (e) recommendations: store layout optimization, signage improvement, department staffing realignment

VP Store Operations and VP Merchandising review findings: (a) incorporate into planogram optimization (W1848), (b) address navigation and signage issues, (c) adjust department staffing based on traffic patterns, (d) consider store layout modifications for high-friction areas

fields.Participants: Market Research Analyst, Category Manager, VP Merchandising

workflows.name: Post-Purchase Experience Survey & Product Satisfaction Tracking

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-file of "System sends post-purchase survey 7 days after transaction" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "review" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-escalate of "escalate to QA Manager per W1839" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-373 (ensure controlled execution — Customer Satisfaction & Experience Research (PA-44.1).)
- operational: Market Research Analyst review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Low response rate**: Most customers don't respond to post-purchase emails; loyalty point incentives improve response rate
Staffing Implication: - No incremental headcount — absorbed by Market Research Analyst
System Touchpoints: - Automated post-purchase survey triggered by transaction event (W1906.1)
- Product satisfaction analytics by SKU with return rate correlation (W1906.2)
- Integration with W12 (returns), W1839 (private label quality), W679 (assortment optimization)

steps.activity: System sends post-purchase survey 7 days after transaction: (a) email to loyalty members and online customers, (b) SMS to POS customers with mobile number on file, (c) questions: (i) "Are you satisfied with the product(s) you purchased?", (ii) "Did the product meet your expectations?", (iii) "Would you recommend this product to a friend?", (iv) "Any issues or concerns with the product?", (v) product-specific questions based on category (e.g., "How is the paint coverage?" for paint, "How is the tool durability?" for power tools)

Monthly analysis: (a) product satisfaction score by category and SKU, (b) identify SKUs with satisfaction score < 3.5/5.0 for Category Manager review, (c) product return correlation: are low-satisfaction SKUs also returned more frequently?, (d) feed into private label quality monitoring (W1839) for BuildRight-branded products

Quarterly: Category Manager reviews product satisfaction data: (a) national brand products with low satisfaction: discuss with vendor, consider alternative products, (b) private label products with low satisfaction: escalate to QA Manager per W1839, (c) customer satisfaction trends inform assortment decisions per W679 (assortment optimization)

fields.Participants: Market Research Analyst, VP Store Operations, Category Manager, VP Merchandising

workflows.name: Customer Complaint Root Cause Analysis & Voice of Customer (VOC) Integration

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-capture of "center complaints" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "Root cause analysis" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-track of "track corrective action effectiveness" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-373 (ensure controlled execution — Customer Satisfaction & Experience Research (PA-44.1).)
- operational: Market Research Analyst review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Social media complaint volume**: BuildRight's Facebook page may receive 50–100+ comments/day; without social media monitoring tool, many complaints go unnoticed; invest in social media listening tool
Staffing Implication: - **Market Research Analyst**: Complaint analysis adds ~2–3 days/month — absorbed by dedicated analyst role
System Touchpoints: - Multi-channel complaint aggregation from CRM, call center, social media, and ecommerce (W1907.1)
- Complaint categorization and analytics dashboard (W1907.2)
- Root cause analysis module with Pareto and trend analysis (W1907.2)
- VOC integration dashboard combining CSAT, NPS, CES, complaint, and post-purchase data (W1907.4)
- Integration with W13.1 (customer complaints), W1116 (complaint trend analysis), W1550 (VOC analysis)

steps.activity: Monthly: Market Research Analyst aggregates complaint data from all channels: (a) in-store complaints (logged by CSR per W13.1), (b) call center complaints (logged by customer service), (c) email complaints, (d) social media complaints (Facebook, Instagram, Twitter mentions), (e) ecommerce reviews and ratings, (f) categorize complaints: product quality, pricing, staff behavior, store cleanliness, out-of-stock, delivery, returns, wait time, others

Root cause analysis: (a) top 10 complaint categories by volume and severity, (b) complaint rate per store: identify stores with complaint rates > 2× chain average, (c) Pareto analysis: 80% of complaints from which 20% of causes?, (d) trend analysis: are complaint volumes increasing or decreasing by category?, (e) specific product complaints: SKUs with highest complaint rates for Category Manager review, (f) staff behavior complaints: identify specific stores or departments for targeted training

Quarterly deep-dive: (a) Market Research Analyst presents comprehensive complaint analysis to VP Store Operations, VP Merchandising, and CMO, (b) identify systemic issues (process, training, product, policy) vs. isolated incidents, (c) recommend specific corrective actions with measurable targets, (d) track corrective action effectiveness: did complaint rate decrease after intervention?

VOC integration: (a) integrate complaint insights with CSAT, NPS, and post-purchase data for holistic customer experience view, (b) feed insights into relevant workflows: product quality → W1839, staff training → W41, pricing → W40, inventory availability → W4, (c) monthly VOC summary distributed to all department heads

fields.Frequency: Monthly mystery shopping at ~65–70 stores (rotated quarterly across all 200)
fields.Participants: Market Research Analyst, VP Store Operations, Mystery Shopping Agency, Store Managers
fields.Volume: ~65–70 mystery shops/month (~800/year; each store visited at least once per quarter)

workflows.name: Mystery Shopping Program Execution & Compliance Scoring

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-validate of "Market Research Analyst manages mystery shopping program" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-file of "Mystery shopping agency executes monthly visits" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-distribute of "distribute store-level results to Store Managers" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Mystery shopper detection**: Store associates may recognize repeat mystery shoppers, especially in smaller provincial stores; rotate shoppers and agencies periodically
Staffing Implication: - **Mystery shopping agency cost**: ~PHP 1,500–3,000 per visit × ~780–840 visits/year = ~PHP 1.2M–2.5M/year
System Touchpoints: - Mystery shopping scorecard management and result tracking (W1908.1–3)
- Store-level analytics with trend tracking (W1908.3)
- Score distribution to Store Managers through store manager app (W1908.3e)
- Integration with W67 (store performance), W41 (training), W575 (weekly store review)

steps.activity: Market Research Analyst manages mystery shopping program: (a) engage mystery shopping agency (Philippine-based with nationwide coverage), (b) evaluation criteria: (i) greeting and acknowledgment by Sales Associate, (ii) product knowledge: can associate answer basic product questions?, (iii) store cleanliness and organization, (iv) shelf price accuracy vs. POS price, (v) checkout experience: queue time, cashier friendliness, transaction accuracy, (vi) trade account recognition (if applicable), (vii) BOPIS experience (if applicable), (viii) fitting/estimation service availability (if applicable), (c) scoring rubric: 100-point scale per evaluation

Mystery shopping agency executes monthly visits: (a) ~65–70 stores per month (rotated to ensure all 200 stores covered quarterly), (b) mystery shoppers: mix of profiles (DIY homeowner, trade professional, new customer, returning customer), (c) scenarios: purchase specific item, ask product question, return an item, inquire about special order, (d) results submitted within 48 hours of visit

Monthly: Market Research Analyst analyzes mystery shopping results: (a) overall compliance score by store and trend, (b) scores by evaluation category: identify weak areas (e.g., product knowledge scoring lowest chain-wide), (c) recognize top-performing stores and associates, (d) flag stores with scores < 70% for VP Store Operations intervention, (e) distribute store-level results to Store Managers (confidentially)

Store Manager receives results and implements improvements: (a) address specific deficiencies identified in mystery shop report, (b) recognize associates who scored well, (c) retrain associates who scored poorly in specific areas, (d) target improvement in next quarter's mystery shop

fields.Participants: VP Store Operations, Market Research Analyst, Store Managers, Regional Managers

workflows.name: Store-Level Customer Experience Benchmarking & Improvement Action Planning

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-generate of "generates store-level CX benchmark report" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "review CX scorecard with each Store Manager and Regional Manager" (replaces manual Step 2).
Controls: - CTL-373 (ensure controlled execution — Customer Satisfaction & Experience Research (PA-44.1).)
- operational: VP Store Operations review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Metric gaming**: Store Managers may focus on improving survey scores rather than actual customer experience (e.g., selectively inviting satisfied customers to respond); ensure data collection is randomized and representative
Staffing Implication: - No incremental headcount — absorbed by VP Store Operations and Market Research Analyst
System Touchpoints: - Store-level CX composite scoring dashboard (W1909.1)
- CX trend tracking with ranking and percentile distribution (W1909.1)
- 90-day improvement plan tracking per store (W1909.2)
- Integration with W67 (store performance), W575 (weekly store review), W72 (employee performance)

steps.activity: Monthly: Market Research Analyst generates store-level CX benchmark report: (a) composite CX score per store: weighted average of NPS, CSAT, CES, mystery shop score, complaint rate, (b) rank stores by CX score: top 20 and bottom 20, (c) trend: improving or declining vs. previous month/quarter, (d) identify outlier stores: (i) high sales but low CX (profitable but unsustainable — customer experience will erode sales), (ii) low sales but high CX (room to grow sales with improved traffic — good experience foundation)

Quarterly: VP Store Operations conducts CX action planning for bottom 20 stores: (a) review CX scorecard with each Store Manager and Regional Manager, (b) identify specific CX gaps per store: is it staffing, training, facility condition, inventory availability?, (c) develop 90-day improvement plan: specific actions, responsible parties, measurable targets, (d) allocate resources: additional training (W41), facility improvements (W47), staffing adjustments (W34)

Quarterly: VP Store Operations recognizes top 20 CX-performing stores: (a) include in monthly store performance review per W67, (b) financial incentive: bonus for Store Manager and team (PHP 10K–30K), (c) feature in internal newsletter as best practice examples, (d) share improvement techniques with bottom-performing stores
